Utilities & C Compatibility

On this page

Kernel Primitives (std::kernel) ​

std/kernel/ provides the building blocks for writing a small kernel or hypervisor from scratch — physical memory allocation, page tables and MMU context, process control blocks, a round-robin scheduler, IPC mailboxes, and syscall dispatch. All freestanding-safe; this is lower-level than std::hal/std::interrupt, which assume you're writing firmware for a single address space rather than managing multiple ones.

c
#include <std/kernel/frame.h>
#include <std/kernel/process.h>
#include <std/kernel/scheduler.h>

static struct FrameAllocator frames;

void kernel_setup() {
    frames.init(1024);              // 1024 4K frames = 4 MiB tracked
    long long f = frames.alloc();   // -1 on OOM

    struct PCB p = std::PCB::new(1, 0x1000, 0x8000, 0);   // pid, entry, sp, page_table
    struct Scheduler sched = std::Scheduler::new();
    unsafe { sched.spawn_proc(&p); }
    int next = sched.next();        // highest-priority READY process index
}

Physical Frame Allocator (kernel/frame.h) ​

FrameAllocator is a bitmap allocator over 4 KiB frames (FRAME_BITMAP_SIZE = 4096 words = 131072 frames = 512 MB tracked by one instance). init(n), alloc() (frame number or -1 on OOM), free(frame), is_used(frame), mark_range(start, count) (reserve a range up front — e.g. the kernel image itself), free_count(). init clamps n to the 131072 frames the bitmap tracks, and freeing a frame that is already free does nothing. init_at(base, n) starts frame 0 at physical address base instead of 0 — on most Arm and RISC-V boards RAM starts at 1 or 2 GiB — and frame_addr(f) gives frame f's physical address.

Paging (kernel/paging.h) ​

PageEntry (one raw 64-bit entry: physical frame number in bits [63:12], flags in bits [11:0]) and PageTable (512-entry table of them). Flags: PAGE_PRESENT, PAGE_WRITABLE, PAGE_USER, PAGE_WRITE_THRU, PAGE_NO_CACHE, PAGE_ACCESSED, PAGE_DIRTY, PAGE_HUGE. PageTable methods: init(), map(idx, phys_addr, flags), unmap(idx), is_present(idx), get_phys(idx), get_flags(idx), set_flags(idx, flags).

PAGE_SIZE is 4096 bytes and PAGE_TABLE_SIZE is 512 entries per table.

MMU Context (kernel/mmu.h) ​

MmuContext<F: MmuFormat> builds the page tables the CPU itself walks. F is a page-table format type chosen at compile time (the same pattern as BST<K, V, C: Order>'s ordering), one per architecture:

FormatTables
MmuX86_64x86-64 4-level paging, 48-bit VA, 8-byte entries. Non-executable pages set NX, which needs EFER.NXE
MmuX86_32x86 32-bit paging without PAE: 2 levels, 4-byte entries (no NX)
MmuSv39RISC-V Sv39 (RV64): 3 levels, 8-byte PTEs; leaves set A and D up front
MmuSv32RISC-V Sv32 (RV32): 2 levels, 4-byte PTEs
MmuAArch64AArch64 stage 1, 4 KiB granule, 48-bit VA: 4 levels. Leaves use MAIR index 0 for normal memory and 1 for device memory (program MAIR_EL1 with Attr0 = 0xFF, Attr1 = 0x04); TCR_EL1 must select a 4 KiB granule and T0SZ = 16
MmuArmV7ARMv7-A short descriptors: a 16 KiB, 16 KiB-aligned L1 table and 1 KiB L2 tables; normal memory is write-back (TEX=001 C B), device memory TEX=000 B

MmuNative names the format of the CPU being compiled for (there is none on Cortex-M, which has an MPU but no MMU, or on wasm). Every format can be built and walked on any target — on the host for a test or an image builder, say — but activate() and the TLB functions only act when the format is the running bare-metal CPU's; they return 0 otherwise.

c
#include <std/kernel/mmu.h>

static struct FrameAllocator g_frames;

void vm_setup(unsigned long root) {           // a zeroed, 4 KiB-aligned table
    g_frames.init_at(0x80400000UL, 256UL);
    struct MmuContext<MmuNative> m = std::MmuContext::new(root, &g_frames, 0UL);
    m.map(0x80000000UL, 0x80000000UL, MMU_WRITE | MMU_EXEC);   // identity: kernel image
    m.map(0x10000000UL, 0x10000000UL, MMU_WRITE | MMU_DEVICE); // a UART
    m.activate();                             // satp / CR3 / TTBR0
}
  • MmuContext::new(root, frames, phys_offset) (a static method; F is inferred from the declared type): root is the physical address of a zeroed root table (4 KiB aligned; 16 KiB for MmuArmV7), frames a live &static FrameAllocator that supplies one frame per new intermediate table, and the tables are read and written at physical address + phys_offset (0 for an identity-mapped kernel, the direct-map base for a higher-half one).
  • map(virt, phys, flags) maps one 4 KiB page; flags are MMU_WRITE, MMU_EXEC, MMU_USER and MMU_DEVICE (every mapping is readable; RISC-V leaves cacheability to its PMAs). It returns 0 when a table frame can't be allocated or a larger page already covers virt.
  • unmap(virt), walk(virt, &phys_out) (follows larger block/superpage leaves too), and entry(virt, &entry_out) (the raw leaf entry).
  • tlb_flush_all(), tlb_flush_page(virt) and activate(): x86 reloads CR3 / invlpg; RISC-V writes satp (which turns translation on for S and U mode) / sfence.vma; AArch64 writes TTBR0_EL1 / TLBI; ARMv7 writes TTBR0 / TLBIALL. Turning paging on (CR0.PG, SCTLR.M) and the MAIR/TCR setup stay with the boot code.

tests/stdlib/baremetal/qemu/run.sh runs every format on QEMU with translation on — Sv39 and Sv32 from S-mode, AArch64 and ARMv7 with the MMU enabled, x86 32-bit paging and x86-64 long mode — reading and writing a page through an alias mapping.

Page-table formats: MmuFormat ​

MmuContext is a bounded generic struct: its format parameter must satisfy the MmuFormat trait, so a type that isn't a page-table format is an error where MmuContext<...> is named (type 'X' does not satisfy constraint 'MmuFormat' ... (no method 'levels')), not deep inside map().

TraitRequiresSatisfied by
MmuFormatlevels(); shift(l) (the VA bit where level l's index starts, l = 0 at the root); entries(l); esize() (4 or 8 bytes per entry); table_desc(phys) and leaf_desc(phys, flags) (an entry pointing at a next-level table / a 4 KiB page with MMU_* flags); valid(e), is_leaf(e, l), addr(e, l); load_root(root), flush_all(), flush_page(virt) (1 if they ran, 0 if this isn't the running CPU's format). All constMmuX86_64, MmuX86_32, MmuSv39, MmuSv32, MmuAArch64, MmuArmV7 (and so MmuNative)

Every step of map, unmap, walk and entry is a direct, inlinable call to these methods. A new architecture's format conforms by having them; nothing else in mmu.h changes. Code over page tables is written once with the same bound. This builds RISC-V Sv39 tables in a host buffer (the physical address is the host address, so phys_offset is 0) and walks them:

c
#include <std/kernel/mmu.h>

// Written once for every page-table format.
generic<F: MmuFormat>
int map_range(&MmuContext<F> m, unsigned long virt, unsigned long phys,
              unsigned long pages, unsigned int flags) {
    unsigned long i = 0UL;
    while (i < pages) {
        if (!m.map(virt + i * 4096UL, phys + i * 4096UL, flags)) return 0;
        i = i + 1UL;
    }
    return 1;
}

static unsigned char g_mem[17 * 4096];       // 16 frames + alignment slack
static struct FrameAllocator g_frames;

int main() {
    // On the host, build RISC-V Sv39 tables in g_mem (phys == host address).
    unsigned long base = 0UL;
    unsafe { base = ((unsigned long)&g_mem[0] + 4095UL) & ~4095UL; }
    g_frames.init_at(base, 16UL);
    g_frames.mark_range(0UL, 1UL);           // frame 0 is the root table

    struct MmuContext<MmuSv39> m = std::MmuContext::new(base, &g_frames, 0UL);
    if (!map_range(&m, 0x40000000UL, 0x80000000UL, 4UL, MMU_WRITE)) return 1;

    unsigned long phys = 0UL;
    if (!m.walk(0x40002010UL, &phys) || phys != 0x80002010UL) return 2;
    return m.activate();                     // 0: Sv39 isn't this CPU's MMU
}

Process Control Block (kernel/process.h) ​

PCB — pid, state (PROC_READY/PROC_RUNNING/PROC_BLOCKED/ PROC_ZOMBIE), priority, saved stack_ptr/pc, page_table (physical root address), parent_pid, exit_code. PCB::new(pid, entry, sp, page_table); methods set_state, set_priority, save_context(sp, pc), exit(code) (transitions to PROC_ZOMBIE).

Scheduler (kernel/scheduler.h) ​

Scheduler — priority round-robin over up to SCHED_MAX_PROCS (256) PCBs. Scheduler::new(); spawn_proc(&PCB) (returns index or -1 if full), next() (select highest-priority READY process), yield() (mark current READY, select next), block_current(), unblock(idx), remove(idx) (reap a zombie), ready_count(). next() takes the highest priority among READY processes and rotates through equal priorities starting after the current one; remove keeps current on the same process (-1 if it was the one removed).

IPC Mailbox (kernel/ipc.h) ​

Mailbox (via Mailbox::new(owner_pid)) — a fixed-capacity (MAILBOX_CAPACITY = 64 messages, MSG_MAX_SIZE = 256 bytes payload) message queue. send(sender_pid, type, payload, size) (payload is a const ?&unsigned char; pass null with size 0 for a signal-only message), recv(&Message out), peek(&Message out) (non-destructive), has_msg(), length(), clear().

Syscall Table (kernel/syscall.h) ​

SyscallTable (via SyscallTable::new()) — up to SYSCALL_MAX (256) handlers typed fn long long(long long, long long, long long). register_(num, handler)/unregister_(num) (trailing underscore: register is a C keyword), dispatch(num, arg0, arg1, arg2) (returns the handler's result, or -1 if unregistered), is_registered(num).
